paths.description: Homepage and initial consent state; represents discovery, top stories, global navigation, network/security/performance, and preferences.
Politics section listing; represents category/list template and mobile navigation.
Politics article; represents editorial detail, long-form reading, and mobile reflow.
Video article; represents media controls and captions.

findings.summary: No user-preference dark theme
findings.evidence: Under emulated dark preference, the page remains white with dark text; computed color-scheme is normal and CSS inspection finds no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide prefers-color-scheme-driven surface, text, control, and media colors.

findings.summary: No explicit high-contrast or forced-colors adaptation
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no forced-colors or prefers-contrast rules, while Lighthouse found 3.82:1 section-label contrast failures even in the default palette.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast treatment and ensure essential text and controls retain system-visible colors.

findings.summary: Navigation swaps have no View Transition treatment
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across the rendered homepage found no view-transition rules; section navigation is ordinary document navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin section and article navigation with cross-document View Transitions, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Sticky navigation does not expose scroll progress or state
findings.evidence: The 32,118px homepage uses a sticky header, but CSS inspection found no scroll-timeline and no scroll-state-aware treatment or progress cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress/state cue using declarative scroll-driven or scroll-state CSS with fallback.

findings.summary: Consent and subscription wall obscures the primary content on load
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile first-view screenshots show a fixed consent/subscription panel covering most or all news content before any user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep news content readable while presenting a compact, clearly dismissible consent choice; avoid a full-viewport interruption.

findings.summary: Consent modal uses an ad-hoc dialog container
findings.evidence: DOM inspection identifies a DIV with role=dialog rather than a native dialog, and no popover/dialog primitive is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for the modal flow, with correct initial focus, Escape/cancel behavior, and explicit labelling.

findings.summary: Reading is blocked by a consent-or-subscribe detour
findings.evidence: The primary news-reading journey opens behind an unavoidable consent/subscription choice on homepage, section, article, and video templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Let the primary reading flow proceed without a blocking detour and preserve clear, reversible privacy choices.

findings.summary: Largest content appears too slowly
findings.evidence: The trace measured LCP 6.29s; Lighthouse under simulated mobile conditions measured LCP 20.9s, FCP 10.0s, and performance 0.51.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the true LCP resource, reduce critical-path CSS/JS, and defer nonessential consent, ad, and widget work.

findings.summary: Heavy request and script delivery delays content
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 165 requests and 4.34MB transferred, including 66 scripts/1.93MB, 29 stylesheets, and 81 third-party requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer noncritical scripts, reduce third-party startup work, and use effective caching/preload priorities.

findings.summary: Script and third-party payload is disproportionate
findings.evidence: Scripts account for 1.93MB across 66 requests and third parties transfer 1.45MB before the user has chosen a content interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit coverage and third-party value, remove duplicate/unused bundles, and conditionally load advertising and widgets.

findings.summary: Section labels fail minimum text contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports multiple labels at 3.82:1 against #aab9c3, below the 4.5:1 requirement for normal-sized text.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the label color or lighten the strip background to reach at least 4.5:1 in every state.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions and responsive candidates
findings.evidence: Image inspection found all 100 sampled images lacked width/height attributes and 84 lacked srcset; six were oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height (or equivalent intrinsic aspect ratio) and responsive srcset/sizes for every editorial image.

findings.summary: CSP and cookie posture are weaker than expected
findings.evidence: CSP only says upgrade-insecure-requests; one cookie is not Secure and all three sampled cookies use SameSite=None. HSTS and nosniff are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive nonce/hash-based CSP and limit cookie scope; mark every transport cookie Secure and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential.

findings.summary: Large third-party tracking footprint loads around consent
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 20 third-party origins; HAR measured 81 third-party requests and 1.45MB, including Google Tag Manager and profiling/ad vendors.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to minimal collection, gate optional vendors on an affirmative purpose-specific choice, and remove vendors without demonstrated user value.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced policies are absent
findings.evidence: Headers lack Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and both X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors; the CSP contains no script restrictions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy as part of the restrictive CSP rollout.

findings.summary: No offline fallback or installable app surface
findings.evidence: The public news site has no web app manifest and no service-worker registration, so frequently revisited content has no offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a minimal manifest and service-worker offline page, while keeping server-rendered article content as the baseline.

findings.summary: Consent choice visually favors tracking
findings.evidence: The wall gives a prominent “Einwilligen und weiter” action and paid no-tracking option, while rejection is hidden behind “Einstellungen”; it describes processing by 191 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer accept and reject-all with equal prominence, concise purpose-level choices, and equally easy later withdrawal.

findings.summary: Editorial images lack responsive delivery metadata
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 84 lacked srcset, 100 lacked intrinsic dimensions, six were oversized, and ten used legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive modern-format variants and select them with srcset/sizes; retain intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Third-party work consumes a large share of the initial budget
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 81 requests and 1.45MB of a 4.34MB initial load, before a reader engages with content.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and defer optional analytics, ads, offers, and video integrations until consent or interaction.

findings.summary: Homepage heap footprint is large for a news document
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contains 841,061 nodes and 51.27MB self size; after repeated full-page scrolling it remains about 51.51MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile constructors and retained trees, then reduce hydrated widgets, third-party runtimes, and offscreen DOM retained at startup.

taskList.title: Replace the blocking, asymmetric consent wall with equal, content-preserving choices
Reduce and defer critical-path scripts, styles, and third parties to improve LCP
Deploy a restrictive CSP and complete browser security policies
Add preference-driven dark and high-contrast themes
Generate intrinsic, responsive editorial image markup
Progressively enhance navigation and long-page orientation
Add a minimal offline fallback and manifest
